title: Antibiotics designed with generative AI against gonorrhea and MRSA
summary: Over 36 million possible compounds were screened computationally: candidate NG1 killed resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a dish and in a mouse model, while DN1 cleared a MRSA skin infection in mice. Only 2 of 80 fragment candidates could be synthesized; these are preclinical results.

evidence.tested: Generative models screened more than 10^7 chemical fragments in silico against N. gonorrhoeae or S. aureus, plus unconstrained design. Of 24 synthesized compounds, seven showed selective antibacterial activity; two leads reduced bacterial burden in mouse infection models.
evidence.unknown: Mouse results only; no human testing is stated. The paper's abstract was read, not the full text.
evidence.ai_role: Genetic algorithms and variational autoencoders generated fragment-based and de novo compounds; researchers synthesized and tested selected compounds.
